name: Mantle Cell Lymphoma
remarks: This module simulates Mantle Cell Lymphoma (MCL), a rare and aggressive form of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.
MCL represents about 6% of all non-Hodgkin's lymphomas and typically affects older adults (median age 60-65).
The module includes risk factors, symptom progression, diagnostic workup, staging, treatment protocols, and outcomes.
Treatment approaches include chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, and stem cell transplantation.
Prognosis varies significantly based on subtype (indolent vs. aggressive) and molecular markers.
MCL is more common in males (3:1 ratio) and Caucasians.
Risk factors include immunosuppression, autoimmune diseases, and family history.
Mantle Cell Lymphoma onset - typically presents with advanced stage disease
MCL has different variants: conventional, blastoid, pleomorphic, and indolent
